prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key pledges and policies (2019 manifesto)

Brexit and trade
- Pass the existing EU withdrawal agreement, leave in January 2020, negotiate a UK-EU free trade agreement without extending the implementation period beyond December 2020. Outside the single market, customs union and ECJ; no political alignment.
- Pursue free trade deals (target: 80% of UK trade covered within three years), starting with the USA, Australia, New Zealand and Japan; create up to ten freeports.
- Protect UK standards on environment, animal welfare and food; the NHS not included in trade talks.

Economy and tax
- No rises in the rates of income tax, National Insurance or VAT; raise the National Insurance threshold to £9,500 next year and aim for £12,500 longer-term.
- Fiscal rules: public investment to average no more than 3% of GDP; debt interest trigger for reassessment at 6% of revenue; aim to reduce debt by end of Parliament.
- Review and cut business rates (with immediate relief for retail, pubs, small cinemas, music venues); increase Employment Allowance; clamp down on late payments.
- Anti-avoidance law (stronger HMRC unit, tougher penalties); introduce a Digital Services Tax.
- Invest in infrastructure, science and innovation; increase R&D support (tax credit to 13%), create a high-risk research agency; review Entrepreneurs’ Relief.

NHS and social care
- Increased NHS funding; 50,000 more nurses; 6,000 more GPs and 6,000 more primary care professionals; 50 million more GP appointments.
- Build and fund 40 new hospitals over 10 years; roll out cancer diagnostics to 78 trusts; establish an Innovative Medicines Fund.
- Mental health law reform for greater patient control; action on learning disabilities, autism discharge, and gambling addiction.
- Free hospital parking for key groups; increase NHS surcharge and enforcement for overseas users; NHS excluded from trade negotiations.
- Social care: at least £1bn extra annually; cross-party reform with a guarantee no one must sell their home to pay; extend unpaid carers’ leave; double dementia research.

Education and skills
- £14bn extra for schools; minimum per-pupil funding; teacher starting salary to £30,000; arts premium; stronger discipline and Ofsted role.
- £3bn National Skills Fund; 20 Institutes of Technology; upgrade FE estate; attach apprenticeships to major projects.
- Maintain universities’ strength; consider student loan interest reforms; tackle grade inflation.

Work, welfare and families
- Raise National Living Wage to two-thirds of median earnings by 2024 (for over-21s).
- Continue Universal Credit with improvements; end benefit freeze; protect pensioner benefits and triple lock; review net-pay pension anomaly.
- Expand wraparound childcare (£1bn); encourage flexible working; neonatal leave; extend unpaid carers’ leave; reduce disability reassessments and employment gap.

Law, order and security
- Recruit 20,000 police; expand stop and search (fair, proportionate); Police Covenant in law; equip with tasers/body cameras.
- Tougher sentencing for serious crimes; knife crime orders; 10,000 more prison places; strengthen NCA; national cyber crime force and a National Crime Laboratory.
- Victims’ Law; Domestic Abuse Bill; online harms legislation; Gambling Act review (incl. loot boxes); action on unauthorised traveller camps.

Housing and communities
- At least one million homes over the Parliament; target 300,000/year mid-2020s; “infrastructure first” planning; community design codes; building safety reforms and cladding removal.
- Support first-time buyers (long-term fixed-rate mortgages; First Homes 30% local discount); leasehold reform; shared ownership simplification.
- Renters’ reforms: abolish “no-fault” evictions; lifetime tenancy deposit.
- Renew Affordable Homes Programme; Social Housing White Paper; end rough sleeping by end of Parliament; stamp duty surcharge on non-residents.

Infrastructure and connectivity
- Major rail and road investment (Northern Powerhouse Rail; Midlands Rail Hub); EV charging network (£1bn); consult on earliest petrol/diesel phase-out; restore some Beeching lines; bus improvements (incl. electric buses); £350m cycling fund; gigabit broadband nationwide by 2025 with £5bn for hard-to-reach areas.

Immigration and integration
- Australian-style points-based system; overall numbers to come down; fast-track routes for NHS and top global talent; equal treatment for EU and non-EU; five-year wait for most benefits; higher health surcharge; protect rights of existing EU residents.

Environment, climate and rural
- Net Zero by 2050; offshore wind to 40GW by 2030; £800m for first carbon capture cluster mid-2020s; £500m to decarbonise energy-intensive industry; £9.2bn for energy efficiency; fracking moratorium unless proven safe; clean air laws.
- Environment Bill with Office for Environmental Protection and legal targets; £640m Nature for Climate fund (75,000 acres of trees/year; peatland restoration); new National Parks/AONBs; plastics and recycling reforms; deposit return scheme; tougher fly-tipping penalties.
- Farming: replace CAP with “public money for public goods”; budget guaranteed over Parliament; expand seasonal worker scheme.
- Fisheries: independent coastal state; sustainable stock plans; support coastal regeneration.

Union, governance and foreign policy
- Strengthen the Union; UK Shared Prosperity Fund (at least matching prior EU funds) across all nations; devolution within England; support for Northern Ireland institutions and unfettered GB-NI trade.
- Constitutional changes: repeal Fixed-term Parliaments Act; update boundaries; retain First Past the Post; voter ID; curb foreign interference; establish a Constitution, Democracy & Rights Commission; safeguard free press (repeal s.40; no Leveson 2).
- Defence: exceed 2% GDP; real-terms growth; modernise forces; maintain nuclear deterrent; Space Command; support veterans (legal protections, childcare, railcard, NI relief for employers).
- International development: retain 0.7% GNI; girls’ education; Magnitsky-style sanctions; tackle modern slavery; end preventable maternal/newborn/child deaths by 2030; support persecuted groups; UK Holocaust Memorial.

Animal welfare
- Tougher cruelty sentences; crack down on puppy smuggling; animal sentience law; end long live-transport for slaughter/fattening; extend ivory ban; ban primates as pets; measures on cat protection including tackling theft.
